source.title: Loss Surfaces, Mode Connectivity, and Fast Ensembling of DNNs
source.authors: T. Garipov; Pavel Izmailov; Dmitrii Podoprikhin; D. Vetrov; A. Wilson

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Measures train and test error along trained-network paths and compares those outcomes across architectures, datasets, and model sizes; this is conceptual evidence about generalization gaps, not a direct test of the listed original interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about low train loss and test error along paths between independently trained modes, direct line segments between modes, and how connectedness changes with network size. Its FGE ensemble comparisons are not results about the claim's generalization-gap versions and are not included as rows. Cited findings from other work are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures mode connectivity, loss and error along fitted paths, and ensemble performance. None tests V1–V8. Its width sweep measures training-loss barriers and path length, without held-out performance versus width; its connectivity measurements do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its association with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase correctly captures the connectivity findings, with improved connectivity under increased parameterization specific to the supplementary width experiment. It omits the other main conclusion: the resulting geometric insights motivate Fast Geometric Ensembling, which improves ensemble performance over Snapshot Ensembles on the tested benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a curve between independently trained modes and measures loss and error along that path; it does not test the original sources' random-label, width-generalization, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or memorized-example interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The direct line segment between modes has substantially higher error than the trained Bezier and polygonal paths. In the width sweep, increasing fully connected layer size reduces the difference between worst curve loss and endpoint loss and decreases the curve-to-segment length ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned paths connect independently trained networks with generally low training loss and test error, whereas direct segments often have large barriers. Constancy varies: the CIFAR-10 Wide ResNet polychain spans 4.38–10.38% test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained neural-network solutions can be connected by learned simple paths with much lower loss and error barriers than direct interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing fully connected layer widths reduces the excess worst training loss along fitted Bezier curves and monotonically decreases their curve-to-segment length ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater parameterization can improve measured mode connectivity without establishing how held-out error changes with width.

record.problems: The width experiment reports plotted values without numerical values in the text. The measured curve error is not the training-to-test gap named in the supplied versions. Some supplementary tabular layout is flattened, but the metric and curve columns are recoverable from the headers and accompanying prose.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. FGE ensemble accuracy comparisons were excluded because they do not measure the claim's generalization-gap versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training using the same recipe.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. Related-work statements about flatness and large batches are cited background, not this study's tests. Low-loss connecting paths do not establish V7: directional connectivity does not measure magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance. No results bearing on V1–V8 are missing.

versions.untested_parts: Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error under matched standard training.
Large versus small batch size under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
